::: {#exr-miller-taylor-sqrt}
#### Taylor expansion of the square root

Find the first three terms (up to degree 2) of the Taylor series for

$$f(x) = \sqrt{x}$$

at $x_0 = 1/3$.
:::

::: {#sol-miller-taylor-sqrt}
Compute the values at $x_0 = 1/3$:

$$\ba
f(1/3) &= \paren{\frac{1}{3}}^{1/2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}
\\
f'(x) &= \frac{1}{2}x^{-1/2} \implies f'(1/3) = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}
\\
f''(x) &= -\frac{1}{4}x^{-3/2} \implies f''(1/3) = -\frac{1}{4} \cd 3\sqrt{3} = -\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}
\ea$$

The degree-2 Taylor polynomial is:

$$P_2(x) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\paren{x - \frac{1}{3}} - \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{8}\paren{x - \frac{1}{3}}^2$$
:::
